newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican police search suspected ranch of drug baron.
newsitem.headline: Mexican police search suspected ranch of drug baron.

text.p: Mexican police searched a luxury ranch near the southern city of Cuernavaca that was suspected of belonging to alleged drug kingpin Amado Carillo Fuentes, the attorney general's office said late on Monday.

It said detectives received a warrant to enter the house, in the village of Tetecala, some 25 miles (40 km) outside Cuernavaca. They appeared to have found little besides "well-bred horses and ornate animals such as peacocks," the office said.
It said the huge ranch had a closed circuit television system and an electric fence surrounding it.

Carrillo Fuentes has made headlines in Mexico recently because he is alleged to have paid off Mexico's top anti-drugs warrior, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, now jailed on drug corruption charges. The charges against Gutierrez Rebollo have strained Mexico's relations with the United States.
Carillo Fuentes, leader of the powerful Juarez Cartel and Mexico's most-wanted criminal, has been highly succesful at giving police the slip.
In January, he got away when police raided his sister's wedding. Last week soldiers burst into a posh hotel in the central city of Guadalajara looking for him, but he was nowhere to be found.
